label: D2 after a2 led rarely to S1, following a rewarded trial (mid-episode)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (100% of mass), and only when the agent chose a2 and landed in S1 (a rare transition): in_action==2 & in_state==1 gives recall 0.999 but precision 0.22. It also needs the previous trial to have been rewarded (prev_reward==1, 100% of mass; precision rises to 0.34). It also depends strongly on time in the episode: it never fires in trials 0-9 or 70-99 and peaks in trials 20-59. Restricting to ep_trial 15-64 gives dev P 0.61 / R 0.95 / F1 0.75 / mass 0.96. A narrow model-value band (7.13-7.54) works about as well (F1 0.74), so the episode-time effect may reflect a slowly drifting hidden state. It is mostly active when S2 is good (88% of mass), i.e. the rare outcome landed in the bad state, but adding good==2 costs recall and adds little F1. It never fires at D1/GO, after a1, in S2, or after an unrewarded previous trial. The remaining false positives look the same in the observed history. I did not check which variables modulate magnitude. All variables used are observed at D2 (ep_trial is clock time, not a future outcome).
